method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading; exact structural and projected-formula comparison; and replay of both directions of Beth's theorem from the definitions through compactness, interpolation and generalization. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Explicit and implicit definability and the proof of Beth's definability theorem from Craig interpolation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An explicit definition equates an n-place predicate P with an L-formula C having n free variables and not involving P. An implicit definition says that any two P-interpretations on the same L-structure which satisfy the theory must coincide; equivalently, Sigma(P) together with a uniformly renamed copy Sigma(P') entails pointwise equivalence of P and P'.
samples.checks: Arity, free-variable count, language exclusions, universal closures, uniform replacement and the two expansion conditions all retain their source scopes.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Beth's theorem states that Sigma(P) implicitly defines P if and only if it explicitly defines P.
samples.checks: The frozen English omits the second word 'if'; OLFOL-043 restores the complete biconditional in ordinary Marathi prose, matching the proof's two directions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Explicit definability immediately gives implicit definability. Conversely, add constants for the n arguments and use compactness to choose finite Delta-zero and Delta-one. Conjoin the corresponding P and P-prime sentences into D(P) and D(P'), rearrange the entailment so the predicate vocabularies are separated, and apply Craig interpolation to obtain a P-free and P-prime-free C. The two entailments give both directions between P and C; monotonicity and generalization yield the required explicit definition from all of Sigma(P).
samples.checks: The finite subsets, two conjunctions, rearranged entailment, interpolant language restriction, model-renaming equivalence, final biconditional and universal closure were checked formula by formula. OLFOL-044 restores the malformed P-prime atom used before the rearrangement.
